Out of curiosity, as a non American, what's a primary?

Basically it is to determine which candidate each party will run in the general election. Unfortunately US politics is completely dominated by two parties, the Republicans and the Democrats. This makes it virtually impossible for anyone outside of the two parties to be elected president. The Republicans started off with a lot of candidates (I think about 17) but only half of them ever had any sort of a chance. The Democrats started off with 5 candidates and are down to two. Only 4 states have held their primaries so far but a bunch of them have primaries on Tuesday.

How a candidate is selected in the primaries is pretty complicated. Their goal is to gain the support of the majority of the delegates of their party. Each state has a certain number of delegates. These delegates are allocated roughly based on popular support but each state has a different system set up. Some states allocate a proportion of delegates based on what percentage of the vote a candidate gets, others give all of their delegates to the first place finisher. Still other are weird hybrids with very complicated distribution rules. Furthermore their are super delegates who can pledge their support to whoever they want but are generally expected to follow popular vote to some degree.

So yeah, hope that helps a bit.
